subject: botany_2

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.22, printed question 10. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Revised 2026-09-05 after the examiner audit: the insider note and the s2 mistakes line no longer state what a printed answer scores or loses.

insider_note: Two halves, two marks each. The complete answer needs both — four or five advantages AND at least three disadvantages. Split the page down the middle before you start writing.

steps.label: Why transpiration is necessary
steps.margin_note: At least four numbered advantages. Two marks sit here, so do not rush this half.
lines: Transpiration has both benefits and harms, so
it is called a necessary evil.
ADVANTAGES:
1. It creates the transpiration pull that
absorbs and transports water in the plant.
2. It supplies water for photosynthesis.
3. It carries minerals from the soil to every
part of the plant.
4. It cools the leaf surface by evaporative
cooling.
5. It keeps cells turgid, so the plant holds
its shape.
steps.why: Each advantage is a job no other process in the plant does, which is what makes the loss of water unavoidable rather than merely tolerated.
common_mistakes: Listing fewer than four advantages. Two marks need a full list.
Writing only 'it cools the plant'. The transport of water and minerals is the bigger point.
steps.memory_tip: Pull, supply, carry, cool, hold: five jobs one evaporation does.

steps.label: Why transpiration is harmful
steps.margin_note: At least three disadvantages, then one closing line that joins both halves.

lines.text: Necessary for transport, harmful in excess

lines: DISADVANTAGES:
1. Excessive transpiration makes cells flaccid.
2. Flaccid cells slow the growth of the plant.
3. A large amount of water is lost as vapour.
4. Photosynthesis is then limited by the
shortage of water.
So transpiration is necessary for transport but
harmful when it is excessive.
steps.why: The harm is not transpiration itself but its excess, and saying so is what turns two lists into the single sentence the question actually asks for.
common_mistakes: Giving no disadvantages at all. Half the answer is the harm, so the second list has to be there.
Writing that transpiration is useless. The question calls it NECESSARY as well as evil.
steps.memory_tip: Evil only in excess: a little is transport, too much is drought.
